issue.title: sase agent list hides live monitor follow-ups queued for runner capacity
issue.description:
Proposed by agent 14t in DISCOVERED ISSUE note #2 on epic sase-1om (routed there as a
possible owner). Landing agent sase-1om.land confirmed the code path is unchanged on
master a19243cdf6 and that the gap predates the epic (queued branch from 9c167a595b9,
2026-09-06), so it is filed as a standalone bug rather than epic work.

## Symptom

`sase agent list -j` omits a live monitor follow-up turn that is queued for runner
capacity, while `sase agent load` and the TUI capacity inspector (both fed by the Rust
capacity snapshot) list it as a waiter. Repro from 2026-10-27 11:35 EDT on athena:
sase-1ox.1--1 (artifacts ace-run/202610/27/20261027112244, pid alive, waiting.json
slot_requested_at set, agent_session_role=root, parent_timestamp=20261027105002,
launched by monitor te34f57zb1av as monitor_followup_agent) was waiter #1 of 3 in the
authoritative report but absent from `sase agent list -j`.

## Root cause

`is_visible_runner_slot_child` (src/sase/agent/_running_listing_running.py) shows a
non-root record when it is occupying, or when it is queued AND
`is_runner_slot_user_agent_record(record)` is true. That admission predicate
(src/sase/core/runner_slots/_admission_predicates.py) returns False for every
non-parallel record with `parent_timestamp`, and its docstring still claims monitor
follow-ups ride the session slot and never wait. The Rust snapshot disagrees: after the
monitor releases the slot, the follow-up waits and is in `waiters`.

## Suggested fix

`running_from_snapshot` already computes `runner_capacity_snapshot` (in
`_holding_artifact_dirs`). Derive non-root visibility from that snapshot instead of the
Python predicates: show a child row when its accounting state is `holding`,
`riding_claim`, or `waiting`. Then the listing's queued rows equal the report's waiters,
as sase-1om.5 already did for holders. Correct the stale docstring of
`is_runner_slot_user_agent_record`. Keep the TUI and CLI behavior for roots unchanged.
Add a regression test with a queued monitor follow-up record (non-parallel child,
`parent_timestamp`, live pid, `waiting.slot_requested_at`) asserting the list row
exists and matches the snapshot's waiters.

task_type_fields.impact: Agents waiting on capacity vanish from sase agent list and its integrations, which then disagree with sase agent load and the TUI capacity inspector.
task_type_fields.repro: Build a scan with a live non-parallel monitor follow-up record (parent_timestamp set, waiting.json slot_requested_at set, its monitor already released the slot); runner_capacity_snapshot lists it in waiters, but sase.agent.running_listing.running_from_snapshot omits it, so sase agent list -j hides it while sase agent load shows it queued.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1om's landing triage of agent 14t's DISCOVERED ISSUE note #2: the queued-row visibility gap predates the epic and needs its own owner.
